protocol.root: sha256 of the complete canonical byte preimage, rendered as sha256:<64-lower-hex>
protocol.normalization: Unicode scalar sequences are preserved exactly; NFC and NFD are distinct logical text values.
protocol.compatibility: sha256-length-framed-fields-v1 remains a legacy reader protocol and is never reinterpreted as v2.

framing.u64: eight-byte unsigned big-endian, logical input transported as canonical decimal text
framing.i64: eight-byte two's-complement big-endian, logical input transported as canonical decimal text
framing.f64: eight-byte IEEE-754 binary64 big-endian; +0 and -0 remain distinct; NaN and infinities are rejected
framing.text: valid shortest-form UTF-8 scalar bytes, prefixed by byte length; surrogates and malformed UTF-8 are rejected
framing.bytes: raw bytes prefixed by byte length
framing.array: item count followed by canonical items in declared order
framing.set: item count followed by canonical items sorted by unsigned bytewise preimage; equal preimages are rejected
framing.map: entry count followed by text-key/value pairs sorted by the complete encoded text key; equal keys are rejected
framing.record: encoded schema text, field count, then fields sorted by unsigned 64-bit field id; each field is id then typed value

valueSemantics.nullVersusAbsent: null is a value; absent is not encodable. A schema alone decides whether a field may be omitted or has an identity default.
valueSemantics.defaults: no implicit identity defaults; a future default changes the Root-bound schema id
valueSemantics.integerTransport: JSON numbers are not the normative integer model and must not carry Root-bound u64 or i64 values
valueSemantics.floatTransport: the conformance IR carries exact binary64 bits, not decimal JSON spelling
valueSemantics.unicodeEscapes: escape spelling is transport-only; decoded scalar sequence is identity
valueSemantics.schemaEvolution: any field-set, field-type, identity-default, encoding, or meaning change requires a new schema id and new Root
valueSemantics.nonIdentityFields: must be excluded by a closed schema before encoding and never added as unknown fields

schemaRegistry.authority: this machine contract owns schema field ids, order, names and optionality
schemaRegistry.projectionPolicy: C++ and Python keep independent ordered projections; the conformance gate requires exact equality with this registry
schemaRegistry.evolution: any field add, delete, reorder, rename or optionality change requires a new schema id and protocol qualification

orderingRules.rootSets: KFR2 set order over the complete encoded root text; duplicate roots reject
orderingRules.objectVersions: KFR2 set order over a two-item record tuple; duplicate objectId rejects at schema admission even when versionRoot differs
orderingRules.episodeFrontier: KFR2 set order over the complete episodeId/sealedContentRoot/acceptedManifestFrameUid tuple; equal tuples and duplicate episodeId reject

operationRequests.policy: closed mutation request schemas; no extension field is admitted at the top level or in declared nested members
operationRequests.identityBoundary: every admitted request field is either consumed by the action or rejected before requestRoot generation
operationRequests.scope: Fact mutation requests only; query, capability, portability and canonical-root edges keep their own contracts

nested.conditional: mapping_receipt_root is required only for external-identity-with-mapping-receipt and forbidden otherwise

migration.mappingReceipt: binds both protocol labels, both roots, and the exact admission root; it never claims equal bytes or reinterprets the legacy root

conformance.dependencyDriftRule: source and release acceptance must rerun the corpus after JSON, Unicode, hash, compiler, standard-library, or serialization dependency changes
